name: Lonapegsomatropin
lead: Lonapegsomatropin (brand name Skytrofa; development name TransCon hGH) is a once-weekly, long-acting prodrug of growth hormone given by subcutaneous injection. It is used to support growth in height in children whose bodies make too little growth hormone, and to replace the hormone in adults with a deficiency. The US FDA approved it in August 2021 for pediatric growth hormone deficiency (GHD) [2][8].

For a child with GHD, treatment aims at faster growth and a taller final stature than the untreated condition would allow, and replacing a daily injection with a weekly one is intended to make treatment easier to keep up. The US label covers children aged 1 year and older weighing at least 11.5 kg with growth failure due to inadequate endogenous GH secretion, and adults with GHD [10]. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin in treatment-naive and switched children [1][6].
It is a prescription medicine for diagnosed deficiency, developed by Ascendis Pharma [8]. No trial has tested it for height or appearance in people without a deficiency.

paras: Growth hormone deficiency is a condition in which the pituitary gland secretes too little GH for normal childhood growth. Standard therapy has long been daily injections of recombinant human growth hormone (somatropin), and the treatment burden of daily dosing is described by researchers as a factor in missed doses and suboptimal outcomes [1][9]. Long-acting products such as lonapegsomatropin, somatrogon and somapacitan were developed to reduce that burden, and reviews note they may improve adherence and quality of life [2][9].

The US label lists pediatric patients aged 1 year and older weighing at least 11.5 kg with growth failure from inadequate GH secretion, and replacement of GH in adults with GHD [10]. Trials are registered in Turner syndrome, in short stature from GH-sufficient disorders such as idiopathic short stature and small-for-gestational-age, and in achondroplasia [11][12][13].

The label describes it as a pegylated human growth hormone (somatropin) that binds the GH receptor, with direct tissue and metabolic effects and indirect effects through IGF-1, including stimulation of chondrocyte differentiation and proliferation [10]. A modelling paper describes predicting average IGF-1 levels with once-weekly dosing [5].

Lonapegsomatropin consists of unmodified somatropin transiently linked to a methoxypolyethylene glycol carrier, which releases the hormone gradually after injection. The conjugate has a half-life of roughly 25 hours, which is what allows weekly dosing [7]. A 2025 review points out that daily somatropin products are molecularly identical to one another, whereas long-acting growth hormones differ in the moieties or mechanisms that prolong their action, and that lonapegsomatropin is the only long-acting product available in the US and Europe that releases unmodified somatropin [9].

Because IGF-1 rises and falls over the weekly dosing interval rather than staying nearly constant as with daily somatropin, researchers developed a method to predict average IGF-1 levels for dose monitoring in children [5].

The US labels for long-acting growth hormones list warnings including increased mortality in acute critical illness, severe hypersensitivity, increased risk of neoplasms (notably second neoplasms in childhood cancer survivors), glucose intolerance and diabetes mellitus, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism and hypothyroidism [10]. Label pregnancy information notes no available human data for this drug, that decades of published somatropin data have not identified a pregnancy risk, and that rat studies showed no embryo-fetal harm [10].

The phase 3 heiGHt trial (NCT02781727) was a randomized, open-label, 52-week, active-controlled study at 73 sites in 15 countries. It enrolled 161 treatment-naive, prepubertal children with GHD, randomized 2:1 to weekly lonapegsomatropin or an equivalent weekly dose of somatropin delivered daily. Annualized height velocity at week 52, the primary endpoint, was 11.2 cm per year with lonapegsomatropin versus 10.3 cm per year with daily somatropin (P = 0.009), a statistically significant difference that met the trial's non-inferiority criterion [1].

The fliGHt trial examined children switched from daily somatropin to the weekly product [6], and the enliGHten extension reported two-year safety and efficacy [3]. Trial reports of longer follow-up have described sustained height gains in children treated for up to six years [19]. Adult phase 3 trials have completed, including one comparing lonapegsomatropin with placebo and daily somatropin and a long-term study in adults with GHD [14][15][20].

No head-to-head trials of the long-acting products exist, so comparisons come from network meta-analyses. A 2025 analysis of five eligible trials reported statistically significantly higher annualized height velocity and height SDS change at week 52 for lonapegsomatropin than for daily somatropin and somapacitan [9]. A 2024 analysis that compared somapacitan with the other two found no differences at 52 weeks in height outcomes [21], and another network meta-analysis compared long-acting products on height velocity and safety [4]. Reviews summarising these products are also available [7][8]. Post-authorisation safety studies are registered [16][17].

Lonapegsomatropin is prescription-only in the US and EU. The FDA granted it orphan drug designation before approval, and the EU authorised it in January 2022 [18]. Skytrofa is a pediatric endocrinology product and no looksmaxxing community discussion specific to this drug was located.

Trials in other conditions are registered: Turner syndrome, short stature from GH-sufficient causes such as idiopathic short stature and small-for-gestational-age, and achondroplasia, where it is being tested in combination with navepegritide [11][12][13][22]. A phase 2 trial of that combination reported 52-week results in children with achondroplasia in 2026 [23].

card.summary: A weekly prescription growth hormone prodrug for children and adults with diagnosed GH deficiency; no data for height without deficiency.

quick.overview:
Lonapegsomatropin (Skytrofa) is a once-weekly growth hormone injection approved by the FDA in 2021 for children and adults with growth hormone deficiency. Phase 3 trials compared it with daily somatropin.

Trials involve people with a diagnosed deficiency, and none tests it for height in people without one.
quick.mechanism: It is a pegylated growth hormone prodrug that releases somatropin, which binds the GH receptor and acts partly through IGF-1.
quick.risks: The label lists warnings including neoplasm risk, glucose intolerance, intracranial hypertension, fluid retention, hypoadrenalism, hypothyroidism and hypersensitivity. It is prescription-only.
